title: The Superstate USTB instance is listed as Active with no addresses and no rate limits specified at all
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.3.1 files the Superstate USTB Instance Configuration Document under Active Instances, and then defers essentially all of it: the token address (A...3.1.2.2.1) and underlying asset address (A...3.1.2.2.2) "will be specified in a future iteration of the Grove Artifact", as will the `RateLimitID`s (A...3.1.2.3) and every field of both the inflow and outflow rate limits (A...3.1.2.4.1, A...3.1.2.4.2).

Compare the Ethena USDe instance in the same chunk, which publishes a token address, an `ethenaMinter` address and four concrete limit parameters. The contrast shows this is not the Artifact's standard — it is an instance recorded before its configuration existed.

The reassuring half is that the code makes an unconfigured instance inert. `triggerRateLimitDecrease` begins with `require(maxAmount > 0, "RateLimits/zero-maxAmount")` (A...1.3.4), so an unset limit reverts every metered operation against it. The same fail-closed property that makes a zero limit a deliberate kill switch also means USTB cannot actually be transacted.

The unreassuring half is what "Active" then denotes. If a status can be Active while nothing about the instance is specified or operable, the status field is tracking an intention rather than a state, and a reader cannot use the Active list to determine where Grove's capital can currently go. Several other instances in this chunk are partially deferred in the same way — Blackrock BUIDL-I's outflow slope (A...3.1.2.1.2.4.2) and the USDe instance's underlying asset address (A...3.1.4.1.2.2.2) among them.
description: Token address, underlying address, RateLimitIDs and both inflow and outflow maxAmount and slope are all deferred to a future iteration, leaving an Active instance with no usable configuration.
